andrōn, andrōnis m.

noun, third declension

corridor, a passage between two walls

Used of the long airport corridors in Libellus I.

Other words

  • iter, itineris n.

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · M-O s.v. hallway, corridor; Vitr.

    Morgan–Owens prefers it.

  • ambulācrum, ambulācrī n. — a walk planted with trees, beside a house

    noun, second declension · avoid · classical · Plaut. Most. 3.2.69 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 29

    Traupman’s “corridor, hallway”, but in Plautus and Gellius an outdoor walk among trees (Lewis & Short: ante- and post-classical for ambulātiō).

See also landing, airport.
